image_description: A white minibus with a high-roof conversion, parked on a dirt or gravel surface. The vehicle features blue lettering and logos on the side and front. Several people are standing in the background near tents, suggesting an outdoor market or gathering. The image quality is low resolution with visible compression artifacts.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Boxy body shape noticeably shorter than a full-size bus, yet tall enough for passengers to stand or sit upright comfortably.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle clearly exhibits the proportions of a minibus: shorter than a city bus but taller than a standard van due to the high-roof modification.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large windshield and row of side windows along passenger area.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large front windshield is visible, and there is a distinct row of dark-tinted side windows running along the passenger compartment.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Height is substantial, with entrance door at front or mid-body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle has significant height. While the specific door mechanism isn't fully open, the panel lines on the side indicate a sliding door location typical for this class.
Vertical seams consistent with a sliding door track are visible on the side of the bus.
The short hood and cab-over design are characteristic of vans/minibuses with front-mounted engines.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rear flat or slightly angled panel with taillights and license plate mount.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the vehicle is occluded by the angle of the photograph; only the front three-quarters are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: White, yellow, or company livery paint with route markings.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bus is white with blue text/logos, fitting the description of company livery.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Standard van-sized wheels with steel or alloy rims.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible front wheel matches the size and style of a standard commercial van wheel.
The window configuration implies seating capacity consistent with the 4-10 passenger range.

artifact_observations.location: Side and front of the minibus
artifact_observations.reasoning: The blue lettering on the side ('...tun...') and front is illegible and morphologically inconsistent with real typography, exhibiting slight melting and irregular character shapes typical of AI generation or severe compression artifacts mimicking AI failure.
The figures in the background lack distinct anatomical definition, appearing as smudged color blobs rather than distinct humans. The tents blend into the background with soft, undefined edges.
Global softness and lack of high-frequency detail suggest either low-resolution upscaling or generative smoothing, particularly noticeable on the wheel rims and window frames.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the vehicle classification despite the low resolution and potential stylistic deviations.
To rigorously analyze the illegible blue text for character-level coherence and detect if it is nonsensical gibberish.
To assess the overall degradation, distinguishing between natural camera blur/compression and AI-specific structural smoothing.
To verify that the wheels are properly connected to the chassis and not floating or melted into the ground, a common failure point.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of the side lettering
Structural integrity of the wheel-to-ground contact
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text on the side of the bus. If the text auditor confirms it is gibberish, this is a strong indicator of AI generation. Also, evaluate if the 'smudged' nature of the background people is due to low resolution (real photo) or structural inability to render limbs (AI). The wheel connection point is critical for structural validity.
